note: Two different lists for two different jobs. `sync_folders` is the short allow-list of .claude/ subfolders the release sync is permitted to copy from at all (everything else under .claude/ is never even considered). `never_sync` is the deny-list applied INSIDE those sync_folders: paths relative to .claude/, matched after normalising backslashes to '/', that the sync step must skip even though they live under an allowed folder (private run logs, memory, research, scratch, machine-local state). `dist_forbidden` is a THIRD, independent list: paths relative to the release tree root (which already has `.claude/` as a prefix) that must never be TRACKED in a published release tree at all, checked by forge-release-check.cjs. Deliberately NOT in dist_forbidden by name: the curated placeholder files the public repo ships on purpose (.claude/FORGE_MEMORY.md, FORGE_TASK_HISTORY.md, FORGE_AGENT_LEDGER.md, FORGE_DECISIONS.md, FORGE_OWNER_PROFILE.json, FORGE_PREF_CANDIDATES.json) — those are excluded from SYNC (so the owner's real, private versions are never overwritten by/into the dist tree) but are allowed to exist in the dist tree as the small placeholders they are. Catching real secret/private CONTENT inside an otherwise-allowed file stays the doctor leak scan's job, not this list's. Codex W2-01: every pattern in BOTH lists is compiled case-insensitively (the `i` flag, applied in forge-release-check.cjs's loadExclusions, not written into the pattern strings here) — Windows treats `.CLAUDE/FORGE-RUNS/x` and `.claude/forge-runs/x` as the same folder, so a case-sensitive pattern was a real escape hatch. Codex W2-02: every dist_forbidden pattern that denotes a private `.claude/` subfolder or file is anchored `(^|/)\.claude/...` instead of `^\.claude/...`, so a private folder nested at ANY depth (a `.claude` tree copied under `plugins/forge/` or `templates/`, for example) is still caught, not just one living directly at the release root. Verified against the real public release tree (`forge-system-public`): the only tracked paths containing a nested `/.claude/` are `global-install/.claude/commands/*.md` and `global-install/.claude/skills/forge-core/**` (legitimate shipped template content) plus `.claude-plugin/...`/`plugins/forge/.claude-plugin/...` (a different folder name, `.claude-plugin`, not `.claude` — never matches the `(^|/)\.claude/` anchor because the literal needs a `/` right after `.claude`); none of those contain a `forge-runs`/`agent-memory`/etc. path component, so the any-depth fix adds zero new false positives there. `^_scratch/` stays root-anchored on purpose — it is this project's own root-level scratch-discipline convention (see this project's CLAUDE.md), not a `.claude/` private-folder pattern. WP 1.9: the dated verbatim memory archives (`.claude/FORGE_<NAME>_ARCHIVE_*.md`: memory, task history, agent ledger, decisions) and the distilled `.claude/LESSONS.md` are project memory with NO curated placeholder, so they are dist_forbidden outright (the Boss `agent-memory/**/lessons-archive-*.md` files are already covered by the agent-memory entry). They never reach a release through the sync anyway (root-level `.claude/` files sit outside sync_folders, and the manifest classifies them per-project); this entry is the backstop that turns a tracked copy in a public tree red. WP 2.1: `(^|/)\.forge/` is in BOTH lists. The opt-in `.forge/` state root (forge-paths.cjs, forge-canon.json paths.state_root) holds the same runtime data as the legacy `.claude/forge-*` folders (runs, research, scribe, memory, backups, ...), so it is never synced and never tracked in a release; never_sync already had `^\.forge` (the `.claude/.forge-*` markers), the anchored form also catches a nested `.forge/` folder. Every legacy pattern stays: a matcher must still classify older trees.
